twinstar.job.done.title: Crafting done
gui.twinstar.perf.header.hub: Hub: %s running jobs, %s kinds of items tracked
gui.twinstar.perf.header.how: Java memory of our own data, counted structure by structure (array length × element size + object headers), not the whole game. Checked against a real JVM to within ±10 %. The rating is the worst of these checks:
gui.twinstar.perf.move: Click: fold. Drag the title bar: move the panel. Double-click: back to its place.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.part_patterns.t: Per pattern: its arrays of item ids, amounts and kinds, and the amount objects in them. AE2's own pattern objects are not counted.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.part_items.tip: Per item: level, loop number, cost, best route, and the lists of patterns that make or use it.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.part_bom.tip: The flattened list of raw materials one unit of each item (and one run of each pattern) needs, with log10 amounts.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.part_other.tip: Policy loops, and the layer's own working copy (arrays, price tiers, components) it keeps beside the published version.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.total.tip: Everything above, estimated on the server each time the theory layer changes. It never walks the whole heap.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.per_pattern.tip: Total ÷ number of patterns (their items included). A healthy pack shows about 640 bytes.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.measuring.tip: The size of the newest version is being worked out on the background thread.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.update.tip: Time the theory layer took on the engine's background thread; ⟳ = a full rebuild. %s updates so far, %s of them rebuilds. Last rebuild %s, slowest of the last 8 incremental updates %s.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.churn.tip: Bytes the last update allocated (short-lived objects too), and how many times the data's own size that is. Heavy boxing and copying show up here.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.plan.tip: Of the last %s plans, %s ran into the soft time limit (it stopped improving) and %s into the hard limit (timed out). The latest took %s.
gui.twinstar.perf.theory.growth.tip: How much faster the size grew than items + patterns, since an earlier and smaller version. ×1 = in step (linear); far more means something is not linear or is not let go.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.job.tip: Java memory of this job's own data: inventory, expected returns, tasks and its plan. It tracks %s kinds of items and has %s patterns left.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.all.tip: %s running jobs and the hub's own parts. %s kinds of items are tracked in all.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.pool.tip: Returns waiting inside the hub, the adaptive feeding windows with their timing samples, and what machines hold for the hub.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.per_kind.tip: Memory of the jobs and hub (without the pool) ÷ %s tracked kinds of items. Maps keyed by boxed ids cost 56 to 150 bytes per entry.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.residual.tip: What the hub still held when its last job ended. It should be close to nothing; a lot means something is not released.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.tick.tip: Time the hub's executor took per game tick over the last second with jobs. A game tick is 50 ms.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.alloc.tip: Bytes the executor allocated per second (all short-lived objects included). High means much boxing or copying.
gui.twinstar.perf.hub.old.tip: %s job(s) still run on an older theory version and keep it in memory (about %s in all).
gui.twinstar.perf.check.density: Average per pattern or item kind %s
gui.twinstar.perf.check.churn: Allocated per update: %s the size of the data
gui.twinstar.perf.check.plan_soft: Recent plans at the soft limit: %s
gui.twinstar.plan.force.tooltip: Starts the order although materials or machines are missing: what can be made is made now, the rest is taken from the network as it appears.
gui.twinstar.plan.force.risk: It keeps its black-hole capacity while it waits, and is cancelled (everything returned) after a long time without progress. You can also cancel it on the CPU screen. At most a few forced orders may wait at once.
message.twinstar.forced_timeout: The forced order for %s waited too long for its materials and was cancelled; everything was returned.
